question: A 19-year-old student is struck in the eye by a cricket ball. On examination, a horizontal level of red-coloured material is seen settling in the inferior anterior chamber. A second patient presents with severe corneal ulcer; their anterior chamber shows a similar horizontal level of yellowish-white material. Which statement BEST distinguishes the two findings?

answers.text: Both represent blood in the anterior chamber; the colour difference is due to the age of the haemorrhage

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Incorrect. The yellowish-white material is a hypopyon — composed of leucocytes, fibrin, and inflammatory proteins — not blood. Hyphema contains red blood cells (red/dark red); hypopyon contains white cells (yellow-white). They have distinct aetiologies.

answers.text: The red collection is hyphema (blood from disrupted iris/ciliary vessels); the yellow-white collection is hypopyon (leucocytes from severe intraocular inflammation or infection)

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Correct. Hyphema = blood in the anterior chamber, typically from blunt/penetrating trauma disrupting iris or ciliary body vessels. Hypopyon = sterile or septic leucocyte accumulation, seen in severe corneal ulcers (bacterial/fungal), endophthalmitis, and severe iridocyclitis. Distinguishing colour (red vs yellow-white) and clinical context (trauma vs infection/inflammation) is fundamental.

answers.text: The red collection is a hypopyon from Behçet disease; Behçet characteristically causes shifting red hypopyon

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Incorrect. Behçet disease is associated with a STERILE SHIFTING HYPOPYON — which is yellow-white (leucocytes), not red. The mobile, shifting nature is a classic Behçet feature, but the colour is white/yellow. A red horizontal level indicates hyphema, not hypopyon.

answers.text: Hypopyon is always associated with perforation of the globe; hyphema is always sterile

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Incorrect on both counts. Hypopyon can occur without perforation — it develops in severe corneal ulcers, endophthalmitis, and iridocyclitis where the blood-aqueous barrier breaks down. Hyphema from penetrating trauma is also not sterile if the globe is perforated.

overallFeedback.feedback: Key distinction: Hyphema is red (RBCs — trauma); Hypopyon is yellow-white (WBCs — infection/inflammation). Behçet's hypopyon is characteristically mobile and shifting, but still white — not red.
Correct. Red level = hyphema (blood); yellow-white level = hypopyon (pus/leucocytes). Trauma context vs infection/inflammation context reinforces the distinction.
